paragraph: Teaneck is a single-family town first, with 114 detached sales over six months at a median of $685,000, against 9 condo and townhouse sales, 3 multi-family, and 3 co-op closings. On the single-family side, 68% of homes sold above asking, the sale-to-list ratio is 1.026, and the median days on market is 20. Sellers have the edge here and multiple offer situations are common, though the pace isn't chaotic. Sales ran from $340,000 to $2,997,000, so treat the median as the real guide rather than the extremes. The monthly series tracks the normal Bergen arc and then some: medians climbed from $668,000 in February to $726,000 in July, and June brought 34 closings. If Teaneck follows the usual seasonal pattern, expect volume and medians to ease through fall, but summer has been the strongest stretch. The condo and townhouse tier is thin at 9 sales and a $480,000 median, moving fast at 16 days, though that sample is too small to read as a trend. Co-ops sit lowest at a $171,500 median, and they carry board approval, financing restrictions, and resale friction that not every buyer is aware of going in. If you're comparing tiers, it's about whether you want the space and grounds of a single-family, the low-maintenance setup of a condo, or the lower price point of a co-op.
